findings.name: Prohibited sector
findings.why: Trading in or earning from prohibited goods and services is not permitted.

alternatives: Non-alcoholic grape juice or mocktail menu
Juices, coffee, tea and other non-alcoholic drinks
steps: Stop trading in the prohibited item
Plan the transition and stock sell-off with a scholar's advice
Give income already earned from it to charity

findings.name: Riba (interest)
findings.why: A fixed or guaranteed return on a loan of money is riba and is prohibited.

alternatives: Murabaha (fixed, disclosed mark-up) for equipment or stock
Ijarah (lease) instead of a loan to buy an asset
Musharakah or Mudarabah if you can accept a profit-sharing partner
Qard Hasan (interest-free loan) for small amounts
steps: Do not sign the interest-based contract
Ask an Islamic bank or halal financing provider for a quote
Check that the total cost is fixed and disclosed upfront
If interest was already received, give it to charity without expecting reward
Ask a scholar to review the final contract

findings.name: Maysir (gambling)
findings.why: Gaining or losing wealth purely by chance is maysir and is prohibited.

alternatives: Fixed-price sale of the product
Loyalty points with a defined reward for every purchase
Charity donation drive with no paid chance to win
steps: Stop the chance-based sale or prize draw
Replace it with a fixed-price offer
Give income already earned from it to charity

findings.name: Gharar (excessive uncertainty)
findings.why: Excessive uncertainty about price, subject matter or delivery invalidates a contract. Only excessive gharar is prohibited and scholars differ on the limit.

alternatives: Salam, Istisna or fixed-price supply
Fixed-price contract with a clear delivery date
steps: Fix the price, subject matter and delivery date in writing
Remove open-ended or speculative clauses
Ask a scholar to review the contract
